chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ibn Maskan, from Abu Sa'id, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a man who made a bequest for a hajj and made it a bequest concerning a person.
He said: His executor must bear its cost and place it in a hajj just as he had bequeathed.
For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Then whoever changes it after he has heard it, its sin is only upon those who change it.”

key_terms.أَوْصَىٰ: he made a bequest or will
key_terms.إِثْمُهُ: its sin, the moral burden of the act
key_terms.بِحَجَّةٍ: for a hajj to be performed on behalf of the deceased
key_terms.وَصِيَّةً: a formal bequest stated in a will
key_terms.وَصِيُّهُ: his executor, the one responsible for carrying out the will
key_terms.يَغْرَمُهَا: he must bear its compensation or cost

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an executor who changes a deceased person's bequest for hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a deceased person bequeaths that a hajj be performed, the executor must carry out the will as specified and is liable if he alters it. The cited Qur'anic verse underscores that changing a valid bequest after knowing it is sinful for the one who makes the alteration.
